entry.label: Fractal Enterprise Model and Capabilities
entry.description: Fractal Enterprise Model connects business processes and the assets they use and maintain. The project shows how its notation can represent VSM coordination, recursive operational units and selected enterprise-environment relationships.
entry.canonical_definition: Fractal Enterprise Model connects business processes and the assets they use and maintain. The project shows how its notation can represent VSM coordination, recursive operational units and selected enterprise-environment relationships.

profile.why_it_matters: The diagrams offer a way to inspect concrete processes, assets and responsibilities when a generic organisational model is too coarse.
key_distinctions: FEM notation is distinct from the VSM’s account of viability.
Decomposing a model into variants is distinct from decomposing it into parts.
An installer download is distinct from a tested installation.
practice_connections: Inspect which processes use or maintain an asset.
Use the System 2 and System 1 examples to question coordination and responsibility.
open_checks: Independent validation of the modelling claims remains open.
Platform compatibility has not been tested.
profile.context_and_lineage: Official toolkit and three linked application pages.
profile.editorial_note: Prepared with AI assistance from the specified sources. Publication is authorised; independent specialist review is not recorded. Practice implications are editorial applications.

sources.title: System 2 of VSM through the lens of FEM
sources.notes: Inspected the explanatory text: FEM patterns depict coordination needs and possible System 2 arrangements. The project’s criticism of VSM visual notation is its own assessment.

sources.title: Decomposition of System 1 units of VSM
sources.notes: Inspected text on responsibilities, process/asset boundaries, ghosts and groups. Decomposition may denote variants or parts, which must be distinguished.

sources.title: Structural coupling through FEM
sources.notes: Inspected project account of identifying enterprise-environment couplings. It attributes the term to Maturana and Varela and cites Hoverstadt’s strategy application; those historical claims remain attributed.

sources.title: SCiO SysBoK - Recursion v1
sources.notes: Legacy SCiO SysBoK working presentation; no public link.

sources.title: Recursion - Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures
sources.notes: NIST technical dictionary entry defining algorithmic recursion as a function calling itself on a part of a task, with base and recursive cases. It defines one domain-specific use, not the whole cross-disciplinary concept.
sources.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology

sources.title: Recursive Functions
sources.notes: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry covering recursive definitions, recursive functions, computability and their history. Useful for separating formal recursion from analogy and later organisational uses.

sources.title: Viable System Model - The VSM in 1000 words
sources.notes: Metaphorum explainer identifying Ashby's requisite variety, Wiener's cybernetics and the mathematics of recursive systems among the VSM's theoretical bases. Used as a public bridge source pending exact primary-book locators.

sources.title: Diagnosing the System for Organizations
sources.notes: Stafford Beer's guide to diagnosing organisations with the Viable System Model. The exact primary-book pages for the recursive-system theorem remain to be located before the organisational-recursion relation is promoted.

sources.title: What is the Viable System Model?
sources.notes: SCiO public overview of the VSM as a model of the activities and relationships needed for organisational survival, performance and adaptation.

sources.title: Introduction to Complexity (Santa Fe Institute Complexity Explorer)
sources.notes: Official ten-unit syllabus covering dynamics, chaos, information, self-organisation, agent-based modelling, networks and scaling. Used for curriculum coverage, not proof that the curriculum exhausts complexity science.
